subject: Physics
explanationText: The work done by a variable force F(x) from x1 to x2 is the definite integral W = ∫ F(x) dx. Since F = m(dv/dt) = m*v*(dv/dx), substituting gives W = ∫ m*v dv = (1/2)*m*v2^2 - (1/2)*m*v1^2 = ΔK. This proves the work done by all forces equals the change in kinetic energy.

subject: Physics
topicTitle: Moment of Inertia of a Non-Uniform Rod
explanationText: To find I about one end when linear density λ = k*x: integrate dI = dm * x^2 = (λ dx) * x^2 = k * x^3 dx from 0 to L. This yields I = (k * L^4) / 4. Since total mass M = ∫ λ dx = (k * L^2)/2, we get k = 2M / L^2. Substituting gives I = (1/2) * M * L^2.

subject: Mathematics
topicTitle: Leibniz Rule for Differentiation Under Integral Sign
explanationText: When differentiating I(x) = ∫_{u(x)}^{v(x)} f(x, t) dt with respect to x: dI/dx = f(x, v(x))*v'(x) - f(x, u(x))*u'(x) + ∫_{u(x)}^{v(x)} ∂f/∂x(x, t) dt. Always remember to multiply by the chain rule derivatives of the upper and lower limits!

subject: Chemistry
topicTitle: Crystal Field Splitting in Octahedral Complexes (CFT)
explanationText: In an octahedral field, the 5 degenerate d-orbitals split into two sets: lower energy t2g (dxy, dyz, dxz) stabilized by -0.4 Δo and higher energy eg (dx^2-y^2, dz^2) destabilized by +0.6 Δo due to direct electrostatic repulsion along the Cartesian axes.
